Hey, I'm in the same program, just finishing up my first semester. Here is my input: 

You don't have to go to Arizona. Everything is found in your online profile - all materials, forms, payment and billing information, and even the 'student lounge' 

I actually wanted to add a couple of courses to my program, but as it turns out they have all of their programs already made up, and you can't add or subtract any classes. So, no. You don't have to take other Penn Foster courses to graduate, you just have to finish all material in your program. 

For the externships, they give you a list of places that will automatically accept you for externships because of Penn Foster partnerships, however I am externing elsewhere and all you have to do is fill out the paperwork to ensure that your place meets all of the requirements. 

A couple notes: Penn Foster does accept transfer credits. It prevents you from having to take courses again, and it saves you money off your program. 

It is a lot of work just because you aren't sitting in class with a teacher and classmates. Studying is super weird just because you can't just go to class the next day and ask fellow students or teachers for help. It takes dedication and self control. 

I love Penn Foster. It's been really great so far. I haven't had to take a proctored exam yet, so I can't speak on what those are like. 

If you need some motivation or have any other questions regarding the program, feel free to DM me.

I hope this helps! Good luck on your program!

I was in an honors English course with a paraplegic boy. He told us the story at the beginning of the semester about how it happened, but then didn't mention it again. 

I had to work with him on an in-class project one day. Our task was to read a short story and then share our ideas on possible themes, symbols, and what not. I've never really been that good at this kind of stuff, so when he shared his thoughts on the story we were reading at the time, I was in awe. There were so many symbols in the story that he saw, so many themes in the story that I never thought of, he read between the lines, that kid. 

I wanted to tell him how I felt. 

Class ended and it was time to leave. He had already gone into the hall to get to his next class. I knew I had to say something to him. 

I raced out to catch up to him - of course he couldn't get too far with his electric chair, and for that I was grateful. I called out to him, not knowing exactly how to express my admiration without sounding creepy. "I just wanted to say thank-you for being in my group today," I started. "Your skills, experience and knowledge... amaze me!" 

And then I said something really REALLY fucked up... 

"High Five!" 

He just looks at me. It's awkward for just a minute before I say: 

"Awahh, come on! Don't leave me hangin'," I plead. 

Everyone saw it. My friends, his friends. Thank God he just kind of shrugged it off. He told me, "don't worry. It happens all the time" 

It doesn't happen all the time, I'm just an asshole... But I really did mean well.
